title: x
description: Scrapes posts, and optionally replies, from an X (Twitter) profile or search/hashtag. A date range is a window the run must COVER, not merely filter to: with start_date/end_date and no max_posts, the run collects every post in the range and reports whether it managed to cover it. Needs an authenticated session, forwarded to the Worker as X_SESSION -- logged out, X caps a profile timeline at exactly 5 posts and refuses replies outright, which is an auth-level policy no transport trick lifts.

target.description: A profile handle ('nasa', '@nasa' or an x.com/... URL) or, in hashtag mode, a hashtag ('#space') or any raw search query.

mode.description: What the target names. Defaults to 'profile'. NOTE the two are not equally cheap: a profile is read over plain HTTP (50 posts in about 3 requests), while a search is driven through a real browser page, because X's search endpoint requires a signed header only its own page can mint. Search is also ranked rather than chronological, so a date range filters it rather than covering it.

max_posts.description: Cap on posts returned. OMIT IT when using a date range on a profile: the range is then the stopping condition, and a count here would cut the window short.

start_date.description: Only posts at or after this moment (UTC, inclusive). A bare date means midnight.

end_date.description: Only posts at or before this moment (UTC, inclusive). A bare date means end of day.

collect_comments.description: Also collect each post's replies. Reply paging follows two cursor kinds, so a ranked conversation is walked past its 'show more replies' break rather than stopping there. Roughly 3 seconds per post.

analyse.description: Also produce an AI analysis and report (text, PDF and an HTML dashboard) alongside the data. Defaults to true. Costs two Claude calls; the scrape itself is unaffected either way.

ai_prompt.description: Your own analysis instructions, e.g. 'focus on complaints about delivery times'. Added to the built-in brief rather than replacing it, so the report keeps its structure and always renders.
